clue.text: This puzzle's toppers for 28 occur a couple of ways

parts.note: to be = to exist, to occur
two compass directions, north and south

explanation.surface: A setter boasting that the toast in this grid comes with a topping served twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: each bean in the grid (FLAGEOLET, GREEN, RUNNER, JUMPING, BEANS itself) sits directly above a drinking toast (SLAINTE, PROSIT, SKOAL, BOTTOMS UP), so 28's TOAST comes both ways, the breakfast and the raised glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans on toast is the classic British snack, so beans are what tops toast, and in this grid they literally sit on top of the toasts.

clue.text: Cross new wife gripping groom's head

indicators.note: the new wife holds the letter in her grip, so it goes inside

parts.note: a bride is a newly married woman

explanation.surface: A newly-wed bride, annoyed, clutching her husband's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, the bride's mood; it is the verb, to span. The G slips in just before the bride's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to span a river or gap, as a bridge does.

clue.text: Online program always reflected fruitful growth

parts.note: an applet is a small program run in a web page

indicators.note: a reflection shows a word back to front

explanation.surface: A tech review praising an app that has kept growing steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER for 'always' is a crossword staple from poetry; turned round it gives REE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple tree grows and bears fruit, so it is literally fruitful growth.

clue.text: Films provided to occupy relative

indicators.note: one word moves into the other and fills its middle

explanation.surface: Someone lending money so a relative can take a lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' in the plural is the whole definition: early cinema without soundtracks, known collectively by the adjective turned noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Silents are silent films, the pictures made before sound.

clue.text: ELO perhaps changes direction, inspired by detuned flute

indicators.note: the letters run the other way
breathed in by the outer word, so held inside it

explanation.surface: A band that swaps musical style after hearing a badly tuned flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ELO perhaps' looks like a band given as an example; 'perhaps' is only the abbreviation for 'for example'. ELO is the rock band Electric Light Orchestra, used purely for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small fipple flute, like a tin whistle; it is also a bean, which is why it sits over SLAINTE.

clue.text: Lost backing and received double-digit sum

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: to be for something is to back it
ten is the first number with two digits

explanation.surface: A gambler who lost their stake but took home ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' does its own work here: FOR = in favour of, backing. TEN is the smallest two-digit number.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of gone from memory, as a forgotten name is a lost one.

clue.text: Fools common folks out of millions

explanation.surface: Ordinary people cheated out of millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' looks like the verb, to con people out of money; it is the plural noun. (M)ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the donkey's reputation for stupidity makes an ass a byword for a fool.

clue.text: Time before inevitable cancellation

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The period before an event is inevitably called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' just puts ERA first.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a deletion, the cancelling of something written.

clue.text: Discovered in Whitechapel: an airy veranda?

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An open-air porch turning up in an unlikely part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitechapel is a crowded area of East London, the last place for an airy veranda, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanai is a Hawaiian veranda or open-sided porch.

clue.text: Even you would like hippie clothing

definitions.note: TIE-DYED is an adjective; the definition reads as a noun phrase, the look of the clothing

parts.note: ye'd = you would, with the old ye

explanation.surface: Someone saying that even you would fancy the hippie look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb ('even you'); it is the adjective, level, as in scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyed shirts, patterned by knotting and dyeing, are the classic hippie garment.

clue.text: Thing puncturing another — one's lighter

explanation.surface: A cryptic label on a sharp object that seems to be about a cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's lighter' suggests a lighter belonging to someone; read it as I'M PALER, one (I) is (M) lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: An impaler is something that pierces another thing right through.

clue.text: Tribute done in empty template

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving just the outside letters

explanation.surface: A tribute written on a blank form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' looks like 'filled in', matching the template; it means killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slainte is the Gaelic toast ('health'), a tribute raised with a glass.

clue.text: Party on, in general

indicators.note: one word goes in the other

explanation.surface: Someone telling a crowd to keep partying, in a vague way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'broadly'; 'general' is shortened, as army ranks are in print, and 'on' is the memo-header 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Greens are an environmentalist political party.

clue.text: Vagueness by court is misrepresented

indicators.note: the letters are presented wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a judgment's vagueness has been distorted by the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like the institution doing the misrepresenting; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: writing that is hard to make out is unclear, the fault of meaning both words name.

clue.text: Experts with lovemaking: here's how

explanation.surface: A sex manual promising expert instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here's how' pretends to open an explanation; it is an old drinking toast, like 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin toast, meaning 'may it benefit'; 'here's how' is an old English toast.

clue.text: Guard largely was familiar with recording commercial

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: KNEW, 'was familiar with', minus its W

explanation.surface: A security guard who mostly knew about a record and an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like part of 'familiar with'; KNEW alone is 'was familiar', and 'with' joins the next pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneepad is protective padding, a guard for the knee.

clue.text: How to manage shock? Drink through gallons then rest well

parts.note: kir = white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Advice for coping with a shock: have a stiff drink, then sleep it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright; it is a shock of hair. A kirby grip is the British name for a bobby pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A kirby grip holds unruly hair in place, so it is how to manage a shock of hair.

clue.text: Remarkable people elevated plant and brand making brown sauce

indicators.note: raised up; in a down answer the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: HP Sauce is the best-known British brown sauce

explanation.surface: Celebrities raising a plant and launching a brown-sauce label.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown sauce is a tangy British condiment eaten with a fry-up; HP is its best-known brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is also a person of outstanding ability, a prodigy; the plural covers several such people.

clue.text: Composer mixed up lines and space

indicators.note: things mixed up are jumbled out of their proper order, so the letters of the word come out rearranged

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A composer who has muddled his staff lines and gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: An en (like an em) is a unit of space in printing, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was the Danish composer of six symphonies.

clue.text: Surgery twisted bones to save pair of joints

indicators.note: the letters are bent out of order
the anagram keeps the other piece safe inside it
the first two letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic operation on broken bones, sparing two joints.
explanation.walkthrough: The bones-and-joints surface points to orthopaedics; the surgery is cosmetic. NOSE(JO)B.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for rhinoplasty, the cosmetic operation reshaping a nose.

clue.text: Mute very Republican old lizard

explanation.surface: A description of a silent, old-guard Republican politician as a dinosaur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mute' reads as silent; it is the noun, the device that damps an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sordino is a mute for a stringed or brass instrument.

clue.text: One dashing leader?

definitions.meaning: one who runs things, as a showrunner leads a TV series

explanation.surface: A leader who is also handsome and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashing' looks like handsome; it is running.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who dashes; someone who runs an organisation leads it.

clue.text: Developing perfume across the pond?

parts.note: NA = North America, over the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.surface: A fragrance being developed in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' is British slang for America across the Atlantic; here it gives NA. The question mark flags the loose clueing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, still developing.

clue.text: Stew contains left over bit of broccoli

indicators.note: holds the other letters inside

explanation.surface: A stew with a leftover piece of broccoli in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' and 'left over' paint a kitchen; STEW is the verb, to worry. F(LO)RET.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli's head breaks into small clustered flower-heads, each one of these being a single piece.

clue.text: Short attendant at bank, bright-eyed and bushy-tailed?

indicators.note: cut short, the last letter goes

parts.note: SQUIRE, a knight's attendant, minus its E
to bank on = to rely on

explanation.surface: A short bank clerk who is lively and eager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright-eyed and bushy-tailed' is an idiom for alert and eager; the question mark says take it literally too, like a squirrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirrely means squirrel-like, and a squirrel is literally bright-eyed and bushy-tailed.

clue.text: Peacekeepers and police force not satisfied

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers and police left dissatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a demand or target left unfulfilled, as in 'the conditions were never met'.

clue.text: Creeps pollarded growths around garden

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: hedges grow round a garden; H removed

explanation.surface: Pests crawling through trimmed hedges around a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeps' reads as unpleasant people; it is the verb, edges forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move slowly and carefully, to creep.

clue.text: Southern Aussie native curtailed barroom shout

indicators.note: its tail cut off, the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A cry in a bar from someone from the south of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie native' looks like a person; it is the koala.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoal is a Scandinavian drinking toast, shouted in a bar.

clue.text: Judge American officiating pole vault activity

explanation.surface: A US judge officiating at an athletics meet.
explanation.walkthrough: To ump, short for umpire, is chiefly American usage, hence 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the vaulter clears a high bar, one of athletics' leaping events.

clue.text: Animal sounds like a distraught Scooby-Doo's cry?

indicators.note: says outright that the answer is heard

parts.note: 'oh dear' in Scooby-Doo's R-heavy dog voice

explanation.surface: A cartoon dog, upset, crying out like some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Scooby-Doo, the cartoon Great Dane, starts his words with R ('Ruh-roh'), so his 'oh dear' is 'Roh dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small woodland species of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Small saying in tavern when it's knocked back

definitions.text: Small saying in tavern when it's knocked back

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the tavern
sent back, so the whole thing is read right to left

explanation.surface: A little phrase heard in a pub as a drink goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' does double duty: drinking a glass down, and sending the letters backwards. Read whole, the clue also defines: a short saying heard in a pub as a drink goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Bottoms up' is said as a drink is downed, the glass's bottom tipped up.

clue.text: Add wraps as part of fry-up

indicators.note: folds around the other piece

explanation.surface: Instructions for adding wraps to a cooked breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wraps' looks like the tortilla food, fitting the breakfast; it is the container instruction. 'Add' is the verb as in 'tot up a bill'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is a standard part of a full English fry-up breakfast.
